title: Macrophages in rotator cuff injuries and tendon-to-bone healing: Heterogeneity, pathophysiology, and therapeutic strategies.
snippet: Rotator cuff tears (RCTs) are a leading cause of shoulder disability, with high postoperative failure rates primarily attributed to poor tendon-to-bone healing. Macrophages act as central regulators of the inflammatory and regenerative microenvironment in the injured enthesis, tendon stump, subacromial bursa, and rotator cuff musculature.
